title: LitFM: A Retrieval Augmented Structure-aware Foundation Model For Citation Graphs

problem.claim: LLM-based scientific literature management needs to discern relationships among pieces of scientific knowledge while supporting practical downstream tasks.

gap.claim: Existing approaches often overlook structural and semantic relevance, suffer from hallucinations, and focus narrowly on individual downstream tasks.

contributions.claim: LitFM is a literature foundation model for varied downstream tasks on domain-specific literature, focused on citation information.

LitFM combines a graph retriever with a knowledge-infused instruction-fine-tuned LLM to integrate citation-graph structure, retrieve relevant literature, extract domain-specific knowledge, and reason about relationships.
The work introduces large-scale literature citation benchmark datasets spanning three academic fields with sentence-level citation information and local context.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe LitFM as the first literature foundation model designed for a wide variety of practical downstream tasks on domain-specific literature, and describe its graph retriever as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that integrating citation graphs during training and inference enables generalization to unseen papers and accurate relevance assessment within existing literature.
The authors report a 28.1% precision improvement on retrieval and an average 7.52% improvement over the state of the art across six downstream literature-related tasks.

narrative_sequence.summary: LLMs have made scientific literature management a promising research direction.
Existing methods miss structural and semantic relevance, exhibit hallucinations, and have narrow task applicability.
LitFM combines a citation-focused literature foundation model, graph retriever, and knowledge-infused LLM.
Citation-graph integration supports generalization to unseen papers and relevance assessment.
The work adds citation benchmarks and reports improvements on retrieval and six downstream tasks.

source_observation.claim: Combining graph retrieval with a knowledge-infused LLM is reported to improve citation-aware literature understanding across multiple tasks.

interpretation.claim: Structured relational context may help language models handle knowledge relationships and broaden task applicability.

application.claim: For domain-specific literature systems, jointly modeling citation structure and textual knowledge may support retrieval, relevance assessment, and related downstream tasks.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the reported gains transfer beyond the three benchmark fields or the evaluated tasks.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the model architecture, training procedure, or instruction paradigm details.
The abstract does not identify the three academic fields, baseline systems, datasets, or evaluation protocols.
The abstract does not provide statistical uncertainty, ablations, or independent verification of the reported results.
